subject: psychology
title: Psychological Approaches: Cognitive & Biological
welcome_lead: Inner models and outer biology — two scientific approaches.
meta_desc: A-Level Psychology approaches cognitive schemas information processing biological genes.
final_note: Both approaches are scientific; they differ on what they look.

walkthroughs.body_html: The cognitive approach treats the mind as a computer-like processor. Theoretical models (MSM, WMM) infer mental processes. Schemas (Bartlett's 1932 'War of the Ghosts' study) bias recall — westerners reshaped a Native American story to fit cultural schemas.

The biological approach explains behaviour through genes (heritability of schizophrenia ~80%, Gottesman), brain structure (Maguire's taxi drivers), neurochemistry (serotonin and depression) and evolution (Bowlby's attachment as adaptive). Reductionist but scientific.

Cognitive neuroscience bridges both: PET and fMRI map cognitive processes to brain areas. Posner et al. (1988) showed attention shifts activate the parietal cortex. Tulving (1989) dissociated episodic and semantic memory in prefrontal regions.
